title: Structural evaluation and exchange identities for the actual specialization factors
statement:
Use the finite coefficients $A=A_{E,n}$, lifts, and canonical nearby-cycle maps of [def-trf-deformation-specialization], with the normalized constructible operation datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Let $c:C\to X\times_kX$ be a correspondence of separated finite-type $k$-schemes with a separated finite-type lift $\widetilde c$ over $D=\operatorname{Spec}(k[t]_{(t)})$. Choose the proper refinement $\widetilde c'\to\widetilde c$ and proper extension of $\widetilde c'$ supplied by [lem-trf-specialization-cohomological-comparison]. Write $b'=\widetilde c'_0$, $b=\widetilde c_0$. Let $(f_Z,t_Z,\alpha_g,\beta_g,\iota)$ be either the canonical specialization pre-comparison $c\to b'$ or the proper-direct-image comparison $b'\to b$. These are the actual factors of the canonical comparison, with the maps and finite-Tor domains supplied by that theorem; they are not arbitrary abstract pre-comparisons. Write $\bar c$ for the target of the chosen factor and use the notation $j_Z,r_Z,d_Z,\delta_Z,\Pi$ and the ordinary and exceptional mates of [def-trf-cohomological-comparison]. All the fixed-diagram exceptional operations are assumed admissible as in [def-trf-admissibility]. Then the following structural identities hold on the indicated finite-Tor constructible domains, without assuming that the specialization factor satisfies requirements (VI) and (VII) for every fibrewise proper arrow or has dense special-fibre compactification opens.

For an arrow $g:U\to V$ of the fixed diagram and $M,N\in D^b_{ctf}(V,A)$, use the exceptional tensor and internal-Hom maps $T_g,H_g$ defined by their counit and evaluation transposes in [lem-trf-cohomological-evaluation-calculus].

(a) Exceptional tensor compatibility:
$$\beta_g(M\otimes N)\circ f_U(T_g)\circ t_U\circ(1\otimes\alpha_g)=\bar g^!(t_V)\circ T_{\bar g}\circ(\beta_g\otimes1)$$
as maps $f_Ug^!M\otimes\bar g^*f_VN\to\bar g^!f_V(M\otimes N)$.

(b) Exceptional internal-Hom compatibility:
$$R\mathcal Hom(\alpha_g,\beta_g)\circ r_U\circ f_U(H_g)=H_{\bar g}\circ\bar g^!(r_V)\circ\beta_g$$
as maps $f_Ug^!R\mathcal Hom(M,N)\to R\mathcal Hom(\bar g^*f_VM,\bar g^!f_VN)$.

(c) Tensor unit and diagonal normalization:
$$t_Z\circ(1\otimes j_Z)=1_{f_ZM},\qquad\alpha_\Delta\circ\bar\Delta^*\Pi_{M,N}=t_X,$$
with $f_ZM\otimes A_{\bar Z}=f_ZM$ and $\Delta^*(M\boxtimes N)=M\otimes N$ [def-trf-external-product].



(d) Put $\chi:p_2^*\omega_X\to p_1^!A_X$ for the canonical exchange in the Cartesian square $X\times_kX$ with projections $p_1,p_2$ over $s$ (the leg order is the project's order). More explicitly, put $B_M=(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,a,a}(M))^{-1}:Rp_{1!}p_2^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}a_X^*Ra_{X!}M$, where the compact-support exchange is normalized as in [def-exchange-projection] and is invertible by [prop-functor-package](4). Define $\chi$ to be the $Rp_{1!}\dashv p_1^!$ transpose of $a_X^*(\varepsilon_{a_X,A_s}^!)\circ B_{\omega_X}$. Its barred counterpart is defined by the identical formula for the barred operations. Then
$$\beta_{p_1}(A_X)\circ f_{X\times X}(\chi)\circ\alpha_{p_2}(\omega_X)=p_{1,\bar X}^!(j_X)\circ\bar\chi\circ p_{2,\bar X}^*(\delta_X)$$
as maps $p_{2,\bar X}^*f_X\omega_X\to p_{1,\bar X}^!f_XA_X$.

(e) Exceptional composition: $\beta_{\operatorname{id}}=\operatorname{id}$ and $\beta_{hg}=\bar g^!(\beta_h)\circ\beta_g(h^!(-))$, under the exceptional composition identifications.

Dualizing composition: for every diagram arrow $g:U\to V$,
$$\delta_U=\bar g^!(\delta_V)\circ\beta_g(\omega_V)$$
under $g^!\omega_V=\omega_U$ and $\bar g^!\omega_{\bar V}=\omega_{\bar U}$ of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition].



(f) Let $h:U\to W$, $v:V\to W$, $U'=V\times_WU$, $h':U'\to V$, $v':U'\to U$ form a Cartesian square of arrows in the unbarred fixed diagram, and assume the corresponding barred square is Cartesian. Suppose $h,h',\bar h,\bar h'$ are proper. Let $E:Rh'_*v'^!\xrightarrow{\sim}v^!Rh_*$ and $\bar E:R\bar h'_*\bar v'^!\xrightarrow{\sim}\bar v^!R\bar h_*$ be the right-adjoint fixed-square exchange maps, normalized as mates of compact-support exchange. Then for every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(U,A)$,
$$\bar v^!(\alpha_{h,*})\circ\beta_v(Rh_*M)\circ f_V(E_M)=\bar E_{f_UM}\circ R\bar h'_*(\beta_{v'}(M))\circ\alpha_{h',*}(v'^!M)$$
as maps $f_VRh'_*v'^!M\to\bar v^!R\bar h_*f_UM$. For this last clause, on the specialization factor also require that the total lifts of $h,h'$ are proper. In particular the clause applies to $h=\Delta_X$, $v=c$, $h'=i_F$, $v'=d$ in the fixed square: the total diagonal and its base change are closed immersions. On the proper-direct-image factor the displayed properness of the four fibre maps suffices. These conclusions are structural identities; none asserts compatibility of a trace map or a trace class.

source.place: §4.1.4(b), Lemmas 4.2.1, 4.2.2 and 4.2.4; identities restricted from the proper-total-lift extension, without the erroneous fibrewise-proper assertion

proof.text: First treat the proper-direct-image factor. By [lem-trf-proper-direct-image-comparison], its specified functors, tensor maps, ordinary exchanges, exceptional exchanges and coefficient map form a compactifiable pre-comparison, with the canonical mates. Consequently [lem-trf-cohomological-evaluation-calculus](a)--(d) gives precisely (a)--(d), and [lem-trf-cohomological-exchange-calculus](a)--(c) gives (e),(f). The latter uses only the two Cartesian squares and the four proper fibre arrows assumed in (f). These lemmas use the same counit-defined $T,H,\chi$ and the same mate convention as our statement. No total-lift hypothesis is needed for this factor.

Now take the specialization factor $c\to b'$. By [lem-trf-specialization-cohomological-comparison] it extends to the fixed diagrams of $c^*$ and $\widehat c_0$, with (I)--(V); every total arrow on those extended diagrams is proper, so its proper-total-lift assertion gives (VI) there. These two extended correspondences are proper over $k$. For their own requirement (VII) in [def-trf-cohomological-comparison], use themselves as compactifications, identity open embeddings, and identity restriction isomorphisms. Identity opens are dense, regardless of whether the original special opens are dense. Thus the extended pre-comparison is compactifiable. Apply [lem-trf-cohomological-evaluation-calculus](a)--(d) and [lem-trf-cohomological-exchange-calculus](a),(b) on these extended diagrams. We will restrict those equalities, without applying either theorem to the possibly noncompactifiable original specialization factor.

Write $u_Z:Z\hookrightarrow Z^*$ and $\bar u_Z:Z'_0\hookrightarrow\widehat Z_0$ for the induced opens. The extension of pre-comparisons in [lem-trf-specialization-cohomological-comparison] identifies $f_Zu_Z^*$ with $\bar u_Z^*\widehat f_Z$, including their $t,\alpha,\beta,\iota$. Its open nearby exchanges can equivalently be read from [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange]; these are the canonical exchanges and respect adjunctions. Every $M,N$ on an original object extends to $u_{Z!}M,u_{Z!}N$ in the required domain by [lem-trf-open-ctf], and restricts back by the isomorphism $M\to u_Z^*u_{Z!}M$ of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. No inverse to the lax tensor map is used.

source.place: §4.1.4(b), open restriction of the proper extension

proof.text: Exceptional composition and $u^!=u^*$ give $u_U^*G^!\cong g^!u_V^*$ for an extended arrow $G$ restricting to $g$; the open identifications are those specified in [def-trf-cohomological-comparison] and [def-trf-admissibility]. Internal Hom commutes with open restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Its evaluation restricts too: under the natural tensor--Hom adjunction it is the transpose of the identity, and restriction carries that identity to the identity. Therefore the definitions of $r,j,\delta,\Pi$ as composites or evaluation transposes identify their extended restrictions with the original maps. In particular $u_Z^*\omega_{Z^*}=\omega_Z$ uses exceptional composition for the structure arrow and $u^!=u^*$, as in [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition].

Apply [lem-trf-exceptional-tensor-open-restriction] to the extended $g$ and $\bar g$. Its hypotheses require commutative open squares, not Cartesian ones, so they hold for our diagram opens. It identifies the restrictions of $T_G,T_{\bar G}$ with $T_g,T_{\bar g}$. Since $H$ is their tensor--Hom transpose followed by evaluation, the evaluation identification of the preceding step also identifies $H_G$ with $H_g$. Restrict extended equality (a), evaluating at the extensions of $M,N$ from Step 3, to get (a) on the original factor. Restrict extended equality (b) with those same inputs to get (b). All maps, including $f_U(H_g)$ and the contravariant internal-Hom argument $\alpha_g$, have thus been identified, not just their endpoints.

Restrict the extended tensor-unit equation and the extended diagonal equation of [lem-trf-cohomological-evaluation-calculus](c). Step 4 identifies $j,t,\Pi$ and the diagonal ordinary comparison; pullback composition identifies the two diagonal pullbacks, so their restrictions are exactly (c). For (d), apply [lem-trf-dualizing-projection-open-restriction] separately to $X\hookrightarrow X^*$ and $\bar X\hookrightarrow\widehat X_0$. It states equality of the actual counit-transpose maps $\chi$, with the leg order and inverse compact-support exchange used here. Under these identifications, Step 4 identifies $j_X,\delta_X$, and ordinary and exceptional comparisons restrict by Step 3. Restriction of extended equality (d) therefore gives exactly (d), without claiming that a product open square is Cartesian.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.4(b),(e),(f), restriction of the normalized maps

proof.text: Restrict the identity and composition equations of [lem-trf-cohomological-exchange-calculus](a) on the extended diagrams. The restriction identifications of Steps 3--4 respect exceptional composition, so this gives $\beta_{\mathrm{id}}=1$ and $\beta_{hg}=\bar g^!\beta_h\circ\beta_g h^!$ on the original diagrams. Restrict its clause (b); the restriction of $\delta$ is the original $\delta$ by Step 4, and the dualizing composition isomorphisms are those of [thm-trf-dualizing-complex-composition]. This proves all of (e). Neither equation requires (VI) on an original arrow.

It remains to prove (f) for specialization directly on its original Cartesian square; an arbitrary such square need not remain Cartesian after compactification. Put $L_g=Rg_!$, $R_g=g^!$, $B_g=\beta_{g,!}$ and $A_g=\alpha_{g,*}$. Bars denote the target diagram. By the mate definition [def-trf-cohomological-comparison] and [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], the counit equation for the mate pair $(B_g,\beta_g)$ is
$$\bar\varepsilon_g\circ\bar L_g\beta_g=f_V(\varepsilon_g)\circ B_gR_g.\tag{1}$$
Here both sides run from $\bar L_g f_UR_g$ to $f_V$. The adjunction and triangle identities hold on the finite-Tor constructible domains by [def-trf-admissibility].

source.place: Lemma 4.2.1(c2), counit form of the exceptional mate

proof.text:
Taking mates of the exceptional composition equation of Step 7, by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting](2), gives
$$B_{hg}=B_h(L_g(-))\circ\bar L_hB_g.\tag{2}$$
Composition identifications and associativity are supplied by [prop-functor-package](3). For the two factorizations $vh'=hv'$ this agrees with the composition compatibility of the actual nearby-cycle mates in [lem-trf-nearby-cycle-finiteness-exchange], including when a composite is not separately labelled in the fixed diagram. Put $C:L_vL_{h'}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_hL_{v'}$ for the composition identification, and likewise $\bar C$. Equality (2) for these two factorizations reads
$$f_W(C)\circ B_vL_{h'}\circ\bar L_vB_{h'}=B_hL_{v'}\circ\bar L_hB_{v'}\circ\bar C.\tag{3}$$

The total lifts of $h,h'$ are proper by the extra hypothesis of (f). Thus [lem-trf-specialization-cohomological-comparison] gives $B_h=A_h^{-1}$ and $B_{h'}=A_{h'}^{-1}$, using the proper identifications $L_h=Rh_*$ and $L_{h'}=Rh'_*$ and their barred counterparts from [prop-functor-package](3). Precompose (3) with $\bar L_vA_{h'}$ and postcompose with $A_hL_{v'}$. Cancellation of precisely these two inverse pairs gives
$$A_hL_{v'}\circ f_W(C)\circ B_vL_{h'}=\bar L_hB_{v'}\circ\bar C\circ\bar L_vA_{h'}.\tag{4}$$
No invertibility of $B_v,B_{v'}$ or of a tensor comparison is asserted.

By the final, general Cartesian-square assertion of [lem-trf-trace-map-exchange], the $L_v\dashv R_v$ transpose of $E_M$ is
$$L_vL_{h'}R_{v'}M\xrightarrow{C}L_hL_{v'}R_{v'}M\xrightarrow{L_h\varepsilon_{v',M}}L_hM.\tag{5}$$
It applies because the square is Cartesian, $h$ is proper and all adjunctions are the specified constructible adjunctions. Apply the same assertion to the barred Cartesian square to compute $\bar E$. Only this general normalization assertion is used, not either trace-map compatibility assertion in that node.

Transpose the left side of (f) under $\bar L_v\dashv\bar R_v$. Naturality of the counit first moves $\bar R_vA_h$ outside the transpose. Equation (1) for $v$ then replaces $\bar\varepsilon_v\bar L_v\beta_v$ by $f_W\varepsilon_v B_vR_v$. Naturality of $B_v$ at $E_M$, followed by (5), gives the transpose
$$T_L=A_h(M)\circ f_W(L_h\varepsilon_{v',M})\circ f_W(C_{R_{v'}M})\circ B_v(L_{h'}R_{v'}M).\tag{6}$$
For the right side use the barred formula (5); naturality of $\bar C$ moves $\bar L_v\bar L_{h'}\beta_{v'}$ across that composition comparison. Equation (1) for $v'$ then gives
$$T_R=\bar L_h(f_U\varepsilon_{v',M})\circ\bar L_h(B_{v'}(R_{v'}M))\circ\bar C_{f_{U'}R_{v'}M}\circ\bar L_v(A_{h'}(R_{v'}M)).\tag{7}$$
These are computations with the mate formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] and the exchange normalization of [lem-trf-trace-map-exchange], in the adjunctions of [def-trf-admissibility].

Naturality of $A_h$ at $\varepsilon_{v',M}:L_{v'}R_{v'}M\to M$ gives
$$A_h(M)\circ f_W(L_h\varepsilon_{v',M})=\bar L_h(f_U\varepsilon_{v',M})\circ A_h(L_{v'}R_{v'}M).$$
Substitute this in (6), and then use (4) evaluated at $R_{v'}M$. The result is exactly (7). The adjunction bijection of [def-trf-admissibility] is injective, so the two original maps agree. Under the proper identifications of Step 10 their source is $f_VRh'_*v'^!M$ and their target is $\bar v^!R\bar h_*f_UM$, proving (f).

For the fixed-square instance, the total diagonal $\widetilde X'\to\widetilde X'\times_D\widetilde X'$ is closed because the lift is separated over $D$. Its base change along $\widetilde c'$ is the total $i_F$, hence is closed by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Both total arrows are proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](a), and their generic and special fibres are closed by the same base-change statement. Thus the extra hypotheses used in Step 10 hold for $h=\Delta$, $v=c$, $h'=i_F$, $v'=d$. This completes both factors and all clauses without claiming trace compatibility.

split_report.summary: Proved the structural identities for the actual factors using the proper extension, existing open restriction lemmas and an explicit proper-square mate calculation. Preserved the total-properness caveat and the full statement; no new nodes.
split_report.blueprint: lem-trf-local-term-locality proof paragraphs (1),(2), normal-cone specialization in unit sk-i-curve-zero step 2, via lem-trf-trace-specialization: supplies its structural evaluation and fixed-square identities without the invalid fibrewise-proper inference.

tool_uses.why: Extends arbitrary original finite-Tor constructible inputs to the proper diagrams, without requiring density.
Uses only the open-unit isomorphism recovering an input from its extension.
Generic ringed-site open restriction of derived internal Hom identifies evaluation and its transposes.
Uses only compact-support composition, associativity and its proper-direct-image identification.
Uses only its independent final general Cartesian-square assertion computing the exceptional transpose of right-adjoint exchange.
Generic scheme-theoretic base change of the total diagonal verifies the fixed-square properness hypotheses.
Generic closed-immersion properness verifies the total diagonal and fixed inclusion hypotheses.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q10-c880ca2eb (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all 19 proof deps and 11 stmt deps, unit sk-i-curve-zero, the main-20261015 lem-trf-local-term-locality and Varshavsky §4.1.2–4.1.7 and Lemmas 4.2.1/4.2.2/4.2.4 (pp. 26–33). Compared with the pre-delivery node, the statement, stmt_deps, source and blueprint are unchanged. The delivery has no new nodes, no cycle (only lem-trf-trace-specialization cites the item), and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. The 5 inherited search records are kept and 5 new ones cover LeanSearch, Loogle/LeanFinder and grep; there are no SGA citations. Step 1: p_0 is proper, so the proper-direct-image comparison is compactifiable, and the evaluation calculus (a)-(d) and exchange calculus (a)-(c) are identical to clauses (a)-(f). Step 2: the comparison node gives the extension c^*→ĉ_0 with (I)-(V) and every total arrow proper, hence (VI). (VII) holds with identity compactifications, since c^* and ĉ_0 are proper over k. This makes precise Varshavsky's 'the assertion is local' and avoids his unqualified (VI) claim for specialization. Steps 3-7: restriction uses only commutative open squares (exceptional composition with u^!=u^*). The T, χ and internal-Hom restriction nodes have matching hypotheses; F is open in Fix(c^*); open-ctf covers the special opens. Steps 8-13: I re-derived by hand the counit form (1), mate pasting (2)/(3), the cancellation of B_h=A_h^{-1} and B_h'=A_h'^{-1} only (4), the exchange transpose (5) from the 'Moreover' of trace-map-exchange, and the transposes (6)/(7). They agree by naturality of A_h, and injectivity of the adjunction bijection finishes (f). Step 14: the total Δ is closed because lifts are separated, its base change i_F is closed, hence proper. Edge cases: identity arrows; empty opens; non-Cartesian open squares; D⊔η, which shows fibrewise properness is not total properness, so the extra hypothesis in (f) is real and not a weakening. I accept tool_uses lem-trf-open-ctf, lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization and lem-trf-trace-map-exchange (final Cartesian-square normalization only) as generic black boxes. The other declared tool_uses are on the route or Mathlib leaves. No fixes.
